name: Lightweight RFC
description: A 2–3 page proposal for a small team: simplest viable design, alternatives and open questions.
promptDelta:
Shorten the document into a lightweight RFC (2–3 pages) instead of the full section list.
- Sections: Context, Proposal, Alternatives considered (at least two, including "do nothing" or "buy instead of build", with trade-offs), Risks, Rollout, Open questions.
- Prefer the simplest architecture that meets the stated requirements, and justify every extra service, queue or datastore.
- Say which sections of a full design doc you skipped and why.

name: Architecture Decision Records
description: Also capture the key decisions as ADRs so the reasoning survives after the doc goes stale.
promptDelta:
In addition to the design doc, capture the 3–5 most consequential decisions as Architecture Decision Records. For each:
- Title, Status (Proposed), Context, Decision, Alternatives considered, Consequences (positive and negative).
- Reference the requirement or constraint above that drives the decision.
Put the ADRs in an appendix, one heading per record (in a coding agent, write each to `docs/adr/NNNN-title.md`).

name: Security & threat model
description: Expands security into a STRIDE threat model for products handling sensitive data or facing a security review.
promptDelta:
Expand the Security & Compliance section into a threat model:
- List the assets and trust boundaries, and mark them on the architecture diagram.
- For each boundary, walk through STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege) with a mitigation for each relevant threat.
- Cover data classification, encryption in transit and at rest, secrets management, tenant isolation (if multi-tenant) and audit logging.
- Name compliance frameworks only if the inputs mention them; otherwise list the questions to settle with security and legal.

name: Migration from an existing system
description: For replacing or re-platforming something that already runs in production.
promptDelta:
Assume this design replaces or extends a system already in production. Add a Migration Plan:
- Current-state and target-state diagrams.
- Data migration approach (backfill, dual writes or change data capture) and how to verify the data matches.
- An incremental (strangler-style) cutover sequence, with a rollback plan for each phase.
- Compatibility requirements for existing clients and integrations.
If the current architecture isn't described above, write `[DATA NEEDED: current architecture]` instead of assuming it.
